newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's General Asia Bank expects IPO in May.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's General Asia Bank expects IPO in May.

text.p: New Thai commercial bank General Asia Bank expects to launch an initial public offering in May, the company said in a statement issued on Thursday.
The firm said the Securities Exchange Commission had its application to offer shares to the general public worth 3.75 billion baht ($144.2 million).
"This means within 45 days from now or by May 6 this year, we can expect SEC approval on our application. Then we will immediately offer the IPO shares to potential subscribers," the statement said.
Under Ministry of Finance regulations governing the new bank's public offering, 50 percent of the bank's shares will be offered to the general public.
The firm has proposed to offer 10 percent of its shares to residents of the northeastern city of Khon Kaen, where the bank will locate its headquarters.
The remaining 40 percent will be offered to randomly selected names on a list of 18.5 million eligible people, the firm said.
Subscribers to the public offering can purchase a maximum of 100,000 baht's worth of shares at their 10 baht par value.
The bank will have a total registered capital of 7.5 billion baht, the statement said.

Conditions of the offer and location of the bank's provincial headquarters are part of government plans to encourage development, and redistribute wealth from the Thai capital Bangkok to the provinces.
Two other consortia which won bank licences last year are yet to announce their plans.
